canonical.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of Two Nodes
canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/3. Hard/02. Lowest Common Ancestor.cpp

narrative.title: The Nearest Shared Manager Ruling
narrative.scenario: An HR system stores reporting lines as a binary tree and must settle which manager is the closest common supervisor of two employees. Company policy allows an employee to supervise themselves in this lookup, so if one of the pair reports up through the other, the deeper one's chain wins at their meeting point. The system returns that junction's id for every dispute.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) plus two integers p and q — the values of the two nodes. Node values are unique.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the value of the lowest common ancestor of p and q.
constraints: Both p and q exist in the tree

testCases.explanation: 5 sits in the left wing and 1 in the right, so the root 3 is their meeting point.
4 descends from 5, and a node counts as its own ancestor.

hintLevels: Level 1: Search from the top; the first node that splits the two targets onto different branches is the answer.
Level 2: A node matching either target short-circuits as the witness — that covers the self-ancestor case for free.
Level 3: Bubble non-null results upward: hits on both sides make the current node the LCA; a single side propagates it.
